title: History 11: Audio models: WaveNet to autoregressive music to diffusion music

questions.q: Why does WaveNet use dilated convolutions?
options: To see far back with few layers: 10 layers reach 1024 samples, where plain ones reach 11
questions.answer: To see far back with few layers: 10 layers reach 1024 samples, where plain ones reach 11
questions.why: Dilations of 1, 2, 4 ... 512 reach 1024. The lab measures both numbers, and the paper states the first.

questions.q: Why is MusicGen's call count so far below WaveNet's for the same length?
options: It predicts 50 frames a second of 4 tokens, not 16,000 samples a second
It uses a higher sample rate
questions.answer: It predicts 50 frames a second of 4 tokens, not 16,000 samples a second
questions.why: EnCodec with a stride of 640 at 32 kHz gives 50 Hz: 1,500 steps for 30 s against 480,000.

questions.q: Going from 30 s to 120 s, what happens to the call count of a 30-step diffusion model?
options: It stays the same, while each call gets bigger
questions.answer: It stays the same, while each call gets bigger
questions.why: Calls follow steps and CFG, and not length. The lab asserts this.

options: An autoregressive model writes a code sequence, then a flow-matching DiT renders from its hidden states
It's a vocoder with no model
questions.answer: An autoregressive model writes a code sequence, then a flow-matching DiT renders from its hidden states
questions.why: ar.py loops over frames, then the graph's KSampler runs on the DiT.

questions.q: ACE-Step has an FSQ tokenizer. Is it therefore autoregressive like MusicGen?
options: No: a tokenizer alone doesn't make it so, and its generator class is a diffusion transformer
Yes: FSQ is a language model
It's neither, since it has no model
questions.answer: No: a tokenizer alone doesn't make it so, and its generator class is a diffusion transformer
questions.why: FSQ is a way to round numbers. Where generation happens is what decides it.
